newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q3 late credit card payments 3.48 pct - ABA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q3 late credit card payments 3.48 pct - ABA.

text.p: Late payments on credit cards fell in the third qaurter to a seasonally adjusted rate of 3.48 percent from the second quarter's record 3.66 percent, The American Bankers Association reported Wednesday.

While third quarter credit card delinquencies were up from 3.30 percent in the same period last year, it was the first time in two years that the rate did not increase from the previous quarter, ABA said.

"The drop indicates that banks and consumers have taken steps to control late payments," ABA chief economist James Chessen said. "Slowed consumer spending in the third quarter along with banks' efforts to tighten credit standards and charge off problem consumer loans combined to bring late payments down."
But Chessen said the late payment rate was still high by historical standards. From 1980 through 1995, the quarterly rate never exceeded the third quarter's 3.48 percent.
"We hope that the drop is a sign that consumers are taking control of their finances, rather than just taking a quick breath before hitting the next holiday sale," Chessen said.
A loan is considered delinquent when it is 30 days or more overdue.

By a slightly different measure of late payments, however, the third quarter was the worst since 1980, ABA said. Measuring the dollar value of credit card loans paid late as a percentage of the value of all loans, the rate was 5.03 percent.

That was up from 4.21 percent in the same period last year and 4.61 percent in the second quarter of this year. The previous high was 4.90 percent in the third quarter of 1986. The dollar late payment rate is not seasonally adjusted.
Late payment rates on home equity and auto loans ticked up slightly in the third quarter from the same period last year, ABA said.
Late payments were received on 1.29 percent of home equity loans, up from 1.26 percent in the third quarter of 1995, and on 1.95 percent off auto loans, up from 1.65 percent, ABA said.
